attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the router between node2 and node3, which sit on separate private point-to-point links (10.10.12.0/24 to node2 via eth1, 10.10.13.0/24 to node3 via eth2). Applied a native VyOS QoS HTB shaper (1mbit) on eth2 egress (the node3-facing interface) so traffic from node2 toward node3 is capped at 1 Mbit/s while node3-to-node2 remains unrestricted. Verified with iperf3: baseline unrestricted throughput was ~20 Gbit/s; after shaping, node2->node3 measured ~957 Kbit/s and node3->node2 measured ~1.05 Gbit/s. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time using their native reboot mechanisms; boot_id changes proved real restarts on each node, and post-restart checks confirmed interface addresses, routes, the QoS shaper, connectivity, and the 1 Mbit/s asymmetric cap all persisted and recovered correctly.
